1: Repeat, friends, no other praise, be not hurtful (to yourselves); praise together Indra , the showerer (ofbenefits) when the Soma is effused; repeately utter praise (to him).

A bull rushing (upon his foes), undecaying, like an ox, the overcomer of (hostile) men, the hater (ofadversaries), the venerable, the displayer of both (enmity and favour), the munificent, the distributor of both(celestial and terrestrial riches).
Although these people worship you, Indra , in many ways to (secure) your protection, (yet) may this ourprayer be throughout all days your magnification.

The sages (your worshippers), Maghavan , the overcomers (of foes), the terrifiers of (hostile) people,pass over various (calamities by your aid); come near and bring manysorts of food, and available for ourpreservation.
Wielder of the thunderbolt, I would not sell you for a large price, not for a thousand, nor for tenthousand, nor, opulent bearer of the thunderbolt, for a hundred.

You are more precious, Indra , than my father, or than my brother, who is not affectionate; you, giver ofdwellings, are equal to my mother, for you both render me distinguished on account of celebrity and riches.
Where have you gone? Where, indeed, are you now? Verily your mind (wanders) among many(worshippers); martial, valorous Purandara , come here; the chanters are singing (your praise).

Raise the sacred chant to him who is the destroyer of the cities (of the foes) of his worshipper,(induced) by which may the thunderer come to sit down at the sacrifice of the sons of Kaṇva , and destroy thecities (of their enemies).
Come quickly with those your horses which are vigorous and fleet, and which are traversers of tens, orhundreds, or thousands (of leagues).
I invoke today the all-sufficient Indra , as the milch cow yielding abundant milk, of excellent motion, andeasy to be milked; or, as another (form), the vast-dropping, desirable (rain).
When Sūrya harassed Etaśa , Śatakratu conveyed (to his aid) Kutsa , the son of Arjuni , with his twoprancing horses (swift) as the wind, and stealthily approached the irresistible Gandharva .
He who without healing materials before the flow of blood from the necks was the effecter of there-union, the opulent Maghavan , again makes whole the dissevered (parts).
May we never be like the abject, Indra , through your favour, nor suffer affliction; may we never be likebranchless trees; for, thunderer, unconsumable (by foes) we glorify you.
Neither rash nor irate, we verily glorify you, slayer of Vṛtra , may we propitiate you, hero, for once (atleast) by our praise with great (sacrificial) wealth.
If he hear our praise, then may our libations, flowing through the filter, dropping quickly, and diluted withconsecrated water, exhilarate Indra .
Come quickly to-day to the collected laudation of your devoted friend; may the subsidiary praise ofwealthy (worshippers) reach you, but now I wish (to offer) your complete eulogy.

Extract the Soma with the bruising stones, wash it with the consecrated waters; (for by so doing) theleaders (of the rain, the Maruts ) clothing (the sky with clouds) as with vesture of the hide of the cow, milk, forth(the water) for the rivers.
Whether come from the earth or the firmament, or the vast luminous (heaven), be magnified by this maydiffusive praise; satisfy, Śatakratu , (my) people.
Pour out to Indra the most exhilarating, the most excellent Soma , for Śakra cherishes him who isdesirous of food, propitiating him by every pious act.
May I never, when importuning you in sacrifices with the effusion of the Soma and with praise, exciteyou like a ferocious lion to wrath; who (is there in the world) that does not solicit his lorḍ

(May Indra drink) with invogorated strength, the strong exhilarating ( Soma ) offered with animating(laudation); for in his delight he gives us (a son) the overcomer of all (foes), the humbler of their pride.

The divine ( Indra ), the accomplisher of all aims, the glorified by his foes, gives vast treasures to themortal who presents offerings at the sacrifice, to him who pours out the libation, who hymns his praise.
Come here, Indra , be exhilarated by the wonderful (libatory) affluence and with your fellow-troopers (theMaruts) fill with the Soma your vast belly, capacious as a lake,
May your thousand, your hundred steeds, Indra yoke to your golden chariot, harnessed by prayer, withflowing manes, bring you to drink the Soma .
May your two peacock-tailed, white-backed horses, yoked to your golden chariot, bring you to drink ofthe sweet praiseworthy libation.
Drink you, who are worthy to be glorified, of this consecrated and juicy libation, like the first drinker( vāyu ); this excellent effusion issues for your exhilaration.

May he who alone overcomes (enemies) through (the power of) religious observances, who by piousacts is rendered mighty and fierce, who is handsome- chinned, approach; may he never be remote; may he cometo our invocation; may he never abandon us.
You have broken to pieces the moveable city of Śuṣṇa with your weapons; you who are light havefollowed him; wherefore, Indra , you are in two ways to be worshipped.
May my prayers when the sun has risen, those also at noon, those also when evening arrives, bringyou back, giver of riches (to my sacrifice).

Praise (me), praise (me), Medhyātithi, for among the wealthy we are the most liberal donors of wealthto you; (praise me as one) who outstrips a horse in speed, follows the right path, and bears the best arms.
When with faith I harness the docile horses in the car, (praise me), for the descendant of Yādu ,possessed of cattle, know how to distribute desirable riches.
(Praise me, saying), "He who has presented riches to me with a golden purse; may this rattling chariotof Asaṅga carry off all the treasures (of my enemy)".

(So praise me, saying), " Asaṅga , the son of plural _yoga, has given more than others, Agni , by tens ofthousands; ten times the (number of) vigorous and brilliant oxen (given by him) to me, issue forth like the reeds ofa lake.
Śaśvatī , perceiving that the sings of manhood were restored, exclaims, "Joy, husband, you arecapable of enjoyment".
2: Give of dwellings ( Indra ), drink this effused libation till your belly is full, we offer it, undaunted (Indra), toyou.
Washed by the priests, effused by the stones, purified by the woollen filter, like a horse cleansed in astream.
We have made it sweet for you as the barley-cake mixing it with milk, and therefore, Indra , (I invoke)you to this social rite.
Indra verily is the chief drinker of the Soma among gods and men, the drinker of the effused libation, theaccepter of all kinds of offerings.
(We praise him) a universal kind-hearted (friend), whom the pure Soma , the mixture (of it) made withdifficulty, or other satisfying (offerings) do not displease.
Whom others pursue with offerings of milk and curds as hunters chase a deer (with nets and snares),and harass with (inappropriate) praises.
May the three libations be effused for the divine Indra in his won dwelling, (for he is) the drinker of theeffused Soma .
Three purifying vessels drop (the Soma ), three ladles are well filled (for the libation), the whole isfurnished for the common sacrifice.
You ( Soma ) are pure, distributed in many vessels, mixed at the mid-day sacrifice with milk, and (at thethird sacrifice) with curds, the most exhilarating (Soma) of the hero ( Indra ).
These dsharp and pure Soma libations effused by us for you solicit you for admixture.
Mix, Indra , the milk and Soma , (add) the cake to this libation. I hear that you are possessed of riches.
The potations (of Soma ) contend in your interior (for your exhilaration) like the inebriation caused bywine; your worshippers praise you (filled full of Soma) like the udder (of a cow with milk).
May the eulogist of you, who are opulent, be opulent; may he even, lord of steeds, surpass one who iswealthy and renowned, like you.
( Indra ), the enemy of the unbeliever, apprehends whatever prayer is being repeated, whatever chant isbeing chanted.
Consign us not, Indra , to the slayer, not to an overpowering foe; doer of great deeds, enable us by youracts (to conquer).
Friends devoted, Indra , to you we, the descendants of Kaṇva , having your praise for our object, glorifyyou with prayers.
(Engaged), thunderer, in your recent (worship) I utter no other praise than that of you, the doer of greatdeeds, I repeat only your glorification.
The gods love the man who offers libations, they desire not to (let him) sleep, thence they, unslothful,obtain the inebriating Soma .
Come to us quickly with excellent viands, be not bashful, like the ardent husband of a new bride.
Let insuperable, delay (coming to us) today until the evening, like an unlucky son-in-law.
We know the munificent genitive rosity of the hero ( Indra ); of the purposes of him who is manifest in thethree worlds (we are aware).
Pour out the libation to him who is associated with the Kaṇva (family); we know not any one morecelebrated than the very powerful bestower of numerous protections.
Offer, worshipper, the libation in the first plural ce to the hero, the powerful Indra , the benefactor of man;may he drink (of it).
He who most recognisant of (the merit) of those who give him no annoyance, bestows upon his adorersand praisers food with horses and cattle.
Hasten, offerers of the libation, (to present) the glorious Soma to the valiant, the hero ( Indra ), for (his)exhilaration.
May the drinker of the Soma libation, the slayer of Vṛtra , approach, let him not be far from us; let thegranter of many protections keep in check (our enemies).
May the delightful steeds who are harnessed by prayer bring hither (our) friends ( Indra ), magnified bypraises, deserving of laudation.

Handsome-chinned ( Indra ), the honoured of sages, the doer of great deeds, come, for well-flavoured isSoma; come, for the libations are ready mixed; his (your worshipper) now (invites you) to be present at this socialexhilarating rite.
They who praising you magnify you, Indra , the instrumental tutor of rites, and those (hymns which glorify) youhave (for their object) great riches and strength.
Upborne by hymns, those your praises and those prayers which are addressed to you, all combined,sustain your energies.
Verily this accomplisher of many acts, the chief (among the gods), the wielder of the thunderbolt, hewho has ever been unconquered, gives food (to his votaries).
Indra , the slayer of Vṛtra with his right hand , the invoked of many in many (plural ces), the mighty by mighydeeds.
He upon whom all men depend, (in whom) overwhelming energies (abide), he verily is the delighter ofthe opulent (worshipper).
This Indra has made all these (beings), who is thence exceedingly renowned; he is he donor of food toopulent worshippers.
He, whom, adoring, and desirous of cattle, the protector ( Indra ) defends against an ignorant (foe),becomes a prince, the possessor of wealth.
Liberal, wise, (borne by his won) steeds, a hero, the slayer of Vṛtra , (aided) by the Maruts , truthful, heis the protector of the performer of holy rites.
Worship, Priyamedha , with mind intent upon him, that Indra , who is truthful when exhilarated by theSoma potations.
Sing, Kaṇvas , the mighty ( Indra ), of widely-sung renown, the protector of the good, the desirous of(sacrificial) food, present in many plural ces.

He who, a friend (to his worshippers), the doer of great deeds, tracing the catttle by their foot-marks,being without (other means of detection), restored them to those leaders (of rites) who willingly put their trust inhim.
You, thunderer, approaching in the form of a ram, have come to Medhyātithi, one of the race ofKaṇva, thus propitiating you.
Liberal Vibhindu , you have given to me four times ten thousand, and afterwards eight thousand.
I glorify those two (heaven and earth), the augmenters of water, the originators (of beings), thebenefactors of the worshipper, on account of their genitive ration (of the wealth so given to me).
3: Drink, Indra , of our sapid libation, mixed with milk, and be satisfied; regard thyself as our kinsman, to beexhilarated along with us for our welfare; may your (good) intentions protect us.
May we be offerers of oblations (to enjoy) your favour; harm us not for the sake of the enemy; protectus with your wondrous solicited (protections), maintain us ever in felicity.
( Indra ), abounding in wealth, may these my praises magnify you; the brilliant pure sages glorify you withhymns.
Invigorated by (the praises of) a thousand ṛṣis, this ( Indra ) is as vast as the ocean; the true mightinessand strength of him are glorified at sacrifices, and in the realm of the devout.
We invoke Indra for the worship of the gods, and when the sacrifice is proceeding; adoring him, we callupon Indra as the close of the rite; we invoke him for the acquisition of wealth.
Indra , by the might of his strength, has spread out the heaven and earth; Indra has lighted up the sun;in Indra are all beings aggregated; the distilling drops of the Soma flow to Indra.
Men glorify you, Indra , with hymns that you may drink the first (of the gods); the associated Ṛbhusunite in your praise, the Rudras glorify the ancient (Indra).
Indra augments the energy and the strength of this (his worshipper), when he exhilaration of the Somais diffused through his body; men celebrate in due order his might today as they did of old.

I solicit you, Indra , for such vigour and for such food as may be hoped for in priority (to others),wherewith you have granted to Bhṛgu the wealth taken from those who had desired from sacrifices, wherewithyou have protected prakṣaṇva.
Wherewith you have sent the great waters tot he ocean; such as is your wish-fulfilling strength; thatmight of Indra is not easily to be resisted which the earth obeys.

Grant us, Indra , the wealth accompanied by vigour, which I solicit from you; give (wealth) first of all tohim desirous of gratifying you, presenting (sacrificial) food; give (wealth), you who are of old, to him who glorifiesyou.

Give to this our (worshipper) engaged in celebrating your sacred rites, Indra , (the wealth) whereby youhave protected the son of Puru , grant to the man (aspiring) to heaven (the wealth wherewith) you havepreserved, O Indra, Ruśama , Śyāvaka and Kṛpa .
What living mortal, the prompter of ever-rising (praises), may now glorify Indra ? No one of thoseheretofore praising him have attained the greatness of the properties of Indra.

Who, praising you as the deity, (ever) hoped to sacrifice to you? What saint, what sage conveys (hispraises to yo?) When, opulent Indra , have you come to the invocation of one pouring out libations, of onerepeating (your) praise?
These most sweet songs, these hymns of praise ascent (to you), like triumphant chariots laden withwealth, charged with unfailing protections, intended to procure food.

The Bhṛgus , like the Kaṇvas , have verily attained to the all- pervading ( Indra ), on whom they havemeditated, as the sun (pervades the unverse by his rays); men of the Priyamedha race, worshipping Indra withpraises glorify him.
Utter destroyer of Vṛtra , harness your horses come down to us, fierce Maghavan , with your attendantsfrom afar to drink the Soma .

These wise celebrators (of holy rites) repeatedly propitiate you with pious praise for the acceptance ofthe sacrifice; do you, opulent Indra , who are entitled to praise, hear our invocation like one who listens to what hedesires.
You have extirpated Vṛtra with your mighty weapons; you have been the destroyer of the deceptiveArbuda and Ṃgaya; you have extricated the cattle from the mountain.
When you had expelled the mighty Ahi from the firmament, then the fires blazed out, the sun shoneforth, the ambrosial Soma destined for Indra flowed out, and you, Indra, did manifest your manhood.
Such wealth as Indra and the Maruts have bestowed upon me, such has Pākasthāman, the son ofKurayāṇa, bestowed, of itself the most magnificent of all, like the quick-moving (sun) in the sky.
Pākasthāman has given me a tawny robust beast of burden, the means of acquiring riches.
Whose burden ten other bearers (of loads) (would be required) to convey, such as were the steeds thatbore Bhujyu home.

His father's own son, the giver of dwellings, the sustainer of strength like (invigorating) unguents, Icelebrate Pākasthāman, the destroyer (of foes), the despoiler (of enemies), the donor of the tawny (horse).
4: Inasmuch, Indra , as you are invoked by the people in the east, in the west, in the north, in the south, so,excellent Indra, have you been incited by men on behalf of the son of Anu; so, overcomer of foes, (have you beencalled upon) on behalf of Turvaśa .
Inasmuch, Indra , as you have been exhilarated in the society of Ruma , Ruśama , Śyāvaka and Kṛpa ,so the Kaṇvas , bearers of oblations, attract you with their praises, (therefore) come here.
As the thirsty Gaura hastens to the pool filled with water in the desert, so, ( Indra ), our affinity beingacknowledged, come quickly, and drink freely with the Kaṇvas .

Opulent Indra , may the Soma drops exhilate you, that you may bestow wealth on the donor of thelibation; for taking it by stealth (when given), you have drunk the Soma poured out into the ladle, and havethence sustained pre- eminent strength.

By his strength he has overpowered the strength (of his foes), he has crushed thei wrath by hisprowess; all hostile armies have been arrested like trees (immoveable through fear), mighty Indra , by you.
He who has made his praise attain to you associates himself with a thousand gallant combatants; hewho offers oblations with reverence begets a valiant son, the scatterer (of enemies).

(Secure) in the friendship of you who are terrible, let us not fear, let us not be harassed; great andglorious, showerer (of benefits), are your deeds, as we may behold them in the case of Turvaśa , of Yadu .

The showerer (of benefits) with his left hip covers (the world), no tearer (of it) angers him; the delightful( Soma juices) are mixed with the sweet honey of the bee; come quickly hither, hasten, drink.
He who is your friend, Indra , is verily possessed of horses, of cars, of cattle, and is of goodly form; he isever supplied with food-comprising riches, and delighting all, he enters an assembly.
Come like a thirsty deer to the watering plural ce, drink at will of the Soma , whence, daily driving down theclouds, you sustain, Maghavan , most vigorous strength.
Quickly, priest, pour forth the Soma , for Indra is thirsty; verily he has harnessed his vigorous steeds, theslayer of Vṛtra has arrived.
The man who is the donor (of the oblation), he with (the gift of whose) libation you are satisfied,possesses of himself understanding; this your appropriate food is ready; come, hasten, drink of it.
Pour our, priests, the Soma libation to Indra in his chariot; the stones, plural ced upon their bases, arebeheld effusing the Soma for the sacrifice of the offerer.
May his vigorous horses, repeatedly traversing the firmament, bring Indra to our rites; may your steeds,glorious through sacrifice, bring you indeed to the (daily) ceremonials.
We have recourse to the opulent Pūṣan for his alliance; do you, Śakra , the adored of many, theliberator (from iniquity), enable us to acquire by our intelligence, wealth and victory.
Sharpen us like a razor in the hands (of a barber); grant us riches, liberator (from iniquity), the wealth ofcattle easily obtained by us from you, such wealth as you bestow upon the (pious) mortal.

I desire, Pūṣan , to propitiate you; I desire, illustrious deity, to glorify you; I desire not (to offer)ungracious praise to any other; (grant riches), bestower of wealth, to him who praises, eulogizes, and glorifiesyou.

Illustrious ( Pūṣan ), my cattle go forth occasionally to pasture, may that wealth (of herds), immortaldeity, be permanent; being my protector, Pūṣan, be the granter of felicity, be most bountiful in bestowing food.
We acknowledge the substantial wealth (of the gift) of a hundred horses, the donation made to usamong men at the holy solemnities of the illustrious and auspicious Rājā Kuruṅga.

I, the Ṛṣi ( Devātithi ), have received subsequently the complete donation; the sixty thousand herds ofpure cattle merited by the devotions of the pious son of Kaṇva , and by the illustrious Priyamedhas .
Upon the acceptance of this donation to me, the very trees have exclaimed; (see these ṛṣis) haveacquired excellent cows excellent horses.
5: When the shining dawn, advancing hither from afar, whitens (all things), she spreads the light on allsides.
And you, Aśvins , of goodly aspect, accompany the dawn like leader with your mighty chariot harnessedat a thought.
By you, affluent in sacrifices, may our praises be severally accepted; I bear the words (of theworshipper) like a messenger (to you).
We, Kaṇvas , praise for our protection the many-loved, the many- delighting Aśvins , abounding inwealth.
Most adorable bestowwers of strength, distributors of food, lords of opulence, repairers to the dwellingof the donor (of the oblation).
Sprinkle well with water the pure unfailing pasturage (of his cattle) for the devout donor (of theoblation).
Come, Aśvins , to our adoration, hastening quickly with your rapid falcon-like horses.
With which in three days and three nights you traverse from afar all the brilliant (constellations).
Bringers of the day, (bestow) upon us food with cattle, or donations of wealth, and close the path(against aggression) upon our gains.
Bring to us, Aśvins , riches comprising cattle, male offspring, chariots, horses, food.
Magnificent lords of good fortune, handsome Aśvins , riding in a golden chariot, drink the sweet Soma .
Affluent i sacrifices, grant to us who are opulent (in oblations) a spacious unassailable dwelling.
Do you ever carefully protect the Brahman among men, come quickly; tarry not with other(worshippers).
Adorable Aśvins , drink of this exhilarating, delightful, sweet Soma , presented by us.
Bring unto us riches by hundreds and by thousands, desired by many, sustaining all.
Leaders (of rites), wise men worship you in many plural ces; come to us with your steeds.
Men bearing the clipped sacred grass, presenting oblations, and completely fulfilling (their functions),worship you, Aśvin .
May this our praise today be conveyed successfully to you, Aśvins , and be most near to you.
Drink, Aśvins , from the skin (filled) with the sweet ( Soma ) which is suspended in view of your car.
Affluent in oblations, bring to us with that (chariot) abundant food, so that there may be prosperity inhorses, progeny, and cattle.
Bringers of the day, you rain upon us by the (open) door (of the clouds) the waters of heaven, or (withthem fill) the rivers.
When did the son of Tugra , thrown into the ocean, glorify you, leaders (of rites)? then when yourchariot and horses descended.
to Kaṇva when blinded (by the Asuras ) in his dwelling, you rendered, Na- satyās , effectual aiḍ
Rich in showers, come with your newest and most excellent protections when I call upon you.
In like manner as you protected Kaṇva , Priyamedha , Upastuta, and the praise-repeating Atri .
And in like manner as (you protected) Anshu when wealth was to be bestowed, and Agastya when hiscattle (were to be recovered), and Sobhari when food (was to be supplied to him).
So pariasing you, Aśvins , rich in showers, we solicit of you happiness as great or greater than that(which they obtained).
Ascend, Aśvins , your sky-touching chariot with a golden seat and golden reins.
Golden is its supporting shaft, golden the axle, golden both the wheels.
Come to us, affluent in sacrifices, from afar, come to this mine adoration.
Immortal Aśvins , destroyers of the cities of the Dāsas , you bring to us food from afar.
Come to us, Aśvins , with food, with fame, with riches, Nāsatyās , delighters of many.
Let your sleek, winged, rapid (horses) bring you to the presence of the man offering holy sacrifice.
No hostile force arrests that car of yours which is hymned (by the devout), and which is laden with food.
Rapid as thought, Nāsatyās , (come) with your golden chariot drawn by quick-footed steeds.
Affluent in showers, taste the wakeful desirable Soma ; combine for us riches with food.
Become appraised, Aśvins , of my recent gifts, how that Kaśu , the son of Cedi , has presented me with ahundred camels and ten thousand cows.
The son of Cedi , who has given me for servants ten Rājās , bright as gold, for all men are beneath hisfeet; all those around him wear cuirasses of leather.
No one proceeds by that path which the Cedis follow, no other proud man as a more liberal benefactorconfers (favour on those who praise him).
6: Indra , who is great in might like Parjanya the disributor of rain, is magnified by the praises o Vatsa .
When his steeds filling (the heavens) bear onwards the progeny of the sacrifice, then the pious(magnify him) with the hymns of the rite.
When the Kaṇvas by their praises have made Indra the accomplisher of the sacrifice, they declare allweapons needless.
All people, (all) men bow down before his anger, as rivers (decline) towards the sea.
His might is manifest, for Indra folds and unfolds both heaven and earth, as (one spreads or rolls up) askin.
He has cloven with the powerful hundred-edged thunderbolt the head of the turbulent Vṛtra .
In front of one worshipper we repeatedly utter our praises, radiant as the flame of fire.
The praises that are offered in secret shine brightly when approaching ( Indra ) of their own will; theKaṇvas (combine them) with the stream of the Soma .
May we obtain, Indra , that wealth which comprises cattle, horses, and food, before it be known toothers.
I have verily acquired the favour of the true protector ( Indra ); I have become (bright) as the sun.
I grace my words with ancient praise, like Kaṇva ; whereby Indra assuredly enjoys vigour.
Amid those who do not praise you, Indra , amid the Ṛṣis who do praise you, by my praise beingglorified, do you increase.
When his wrath thundered, dividing Vṛtra joint by joint, then he drove the waters to the ocean.
You have hurled your wielded thunderbolt upon the impious Śuṣṇa ; you are renowned, fierce Indra ,as the showerer (of benefits).
Neither the heavens, nor the realms of the firmament, nor the regions of the earth, equal the thundererIndra in strength.
You, Indra , have cast into the rushing streams him who lay obstructing your copious waters.
You have enveloped with darkness, Indra , him who had seized upon these spacious aggregated(realms of) heaven and earth.
Amid those pious sages, amid those Bhṛgus , who have glorified you, hear also, fierce Indra , myinvocation.
These, your spotted cows, the nourishers of the sacrifice, yields, Indra , their butter, and this mixture (ofmilk and curds).
These prolific cattle became pregnant, having taken into their mouths, Indra , (the products of yourvigour) like the all-sustaining sun.
Lord of strength, the Kaṇvas verily invigorate you by praise; the effused Soma (invigorates) you.
Indra , wielder of the thunderbolt, excellent praise (is addressed to you) on account of your goodguidance, as is a most extended sacrifice.
Be willing to grant us abundant food with cattle; (to grant us) protection, progeny, and vigour.
May that herd of swift horses, which formerly shone among the people of nahuṣa , (be granted), Indra ,to us.
Sage Indra , you spread (the cattle) over the adjacent pastures when you are favourably inclined towardus.
When you put forth your might, you reign, Indra , over mankind; surpassing are you, and unlimited instrumental ength.
The people offering oblations call upon you, the pervader of space, with libations for protection.
The wise ( Indra ) has been engendered by holy rites on the skirts of the mountains, at the confluence ofrivers.
From the lofty region in which pervading he abides, Indra the intelligent looks down upon the offeredlibation.
Then (men) behold the daily light of the ancient shedder of water, when he shines above the heaveṇ
All the Kaṇvas , Indra , magnify your wisdom, your manhood, and, most mighty one, your strength.
Be propitiated, Indra , by this my praise; carefully protect me, and give increase to my understanding.
Wielder of the thunderbolt, magnified (by our praises), we your worshippers have offered to you theseprayers for our existence.
The Kaṇvas glorify Indra ; like waters rushing down a declivity, praise spontaneously seeks Indra.
Holy praises magnify Indra , the imperishable, the implacable, as rivers (swell) the ocean.
Come to us from afar with your beloved horses; drink, Indra , this libation.
Destroyer of Vṛtra , men strewing the clipped sacred grass invoke you for the obtaining of food.
Both heaven and earth follow you as the wheels (of a car follow) the horse; the streams of the Somapoured forth (by the priests) follow (you).
Rejoice, Indra , at the heaven-guiding sacrifice as Śaryaṇāvat; be exhilarated by the praise of theworshipper.
The vast wielder of the thunderbolt, the slayer of Vṛtra , the deep quaffer of the Soma , the showerer,roars near at hand in the sky.
You are a Ṛṣi, the first-born (of the gods), the chief, the ruler (over all) by your strength; you giverepeatedly, Indra , wealth.
May your hundred sleek-backed horses bring you to our libations, to our (sacrificial) food.
The Kaṇvas augment by praise this ancient rite intended (to obtain) an abundance of sweet water.
The mortal (adorer) selects at the sacrifice Indra from among the mighty (gods); he who is desirous ofwealth (worships) Indra for protection.
May your horses, praised by the pious priests, bring you, who are the praised of many, down to drinkthe Soma .
I have accepted from Tirindira, the son of Paraśu , hundreds and thousands of the treasures of meṇ
(These princes) have given to the chanter Pajra three hundred horses, ten thousand cattle.
The exalted (prince) has been raised by fame to heaven, for he has given camels laden with four (loadsof gold), and Yādva people (as slaves).
7: When the pious worshipper offers you, Maruts , food at the three diurnal rites, then you havesovereignty over the mountains.
When, glorious and powerful ( Maruts ), you fit out your chariot, the mountains depart (from their plural ces).
The loud-sounding sons of Pṛśni drive with their breezes (the clouds), they milk forth nutritioussustenance.
The Maruts scatter the rain, they shake the mountains, when they mount their chariot, with the winds.
The mountains are curbed, the rivers are restrained at your coming, for the upholding of your greatstrength.
We invoke you for protection by night, (we invoke) you by day, (we invoke) you when the sacrifice is inprogress.
Truly these purple-hued, wonderful, clamorous Maruts proceed with their chariots in the height aove thesky.
They, who by their might open a radiant path for the sun to travel, they pervade (the world) with lustre.
Accept, Maruts , this my praise, (accept), mighty ones, this my adoration, (accept) this my invocation.
The kine have filled for the thunderer three lakes of the sweet ( Soma ) from the dripping water-bearingcloud.
When, Maruts , desirous of felicity, we invoke you from heaven, come unto us quickly.
Munificent, mighty Rudras , you in the sacrificial hall are wise (even) in the exhilaration (of the Soma ).
Send us, Maruts , from heaven exhilarating, many lauded, all-sustaining riches.
When, bright ( Maruts ), you harness your car over the mountains, then you exhilarate (yourselves) withthe effusing Soma .
A man should solicit happiness of them with praises of such an unconquerable (company).
They who, like dropping showers, inflate heaven and earth with rain, milking the inexhaustible cloud.
The sons of Pṛśni rise up with shouts, with chariots, with winds, with praises.
We meditate on that (genitive rosity) whereby for (the sake of granting them) riches you have protectedTurvaśa and Yadu and the wealth-desiring Kaṇva .
Munificent ( Maruts ), may these (sacrificial) viands, nutritious as butter, together with the praises of thedescendant of Kaṇva , afford you augmentation.
Munificent ( Maruts ), for whom the sacred grass has been trimmed, where now are you beingexhilarated? What pious worshipper detains you as he) adores you?
( Maruts ), for whom the sacred grass is trimmed, it cannot be (that you submit to be detained), for youhave derived strength from the sacrifice, formerly (accompanied) by our praises.
They have concentrated the abundant waters, they have held together the heaven and earth, they havesustained the sun, they have divided ( Vṛtra ) joint by joint with the thunderbolt.
Independent of a ruler, they have divided Vṛtra joint by joint; they have shattered the mountains,manifesting manly vigour.
They have come to the aid of the warring Trita , invigorating his strength, and (animating) his acts; theyhave come to the aid of Indra , for the destruction of Vṛtra .
The birlliant ( Maruts ), bearing the lightning in their hands , radiant above all, gloriously display theirgolden helmets on their heads.
Glorified, ( Maruts ), by Uśanas , when you approach from afar to the opening of the rainy (firmament),then (the dwellers on earth), like those in heaven, are clamorous through fear.
Come, gods, to (show your) liberality at our sacrifice with your golden-footed steeds.
When the spotted antelope or the swift tawny deer conveys them in their chariot, then the brilliant( Maruts ) depart, and the rains have gone.
The leaders of rites have proceeded with downward chariot-wheels to the Ṛjīka (Ārjīka) country,where lies the Śaryaṇāvat, abounding in dwellings, and where Soma is plural ntiful.
When, maruts , will you go with joy-bestowing riches to the sage thus adoring you, and soliciting (you forwealth)?
When was it, Maruts , who are gratified by praise, that you really deserted Indra ? Who is there thatenjoys your friendship?
Do you of our race of Kaṇva praise Agni together with the Maruts , bearing the thunderbolt in theirhands, and armed with golden lances.
I bring to my presence, for the sake of most excellent prosperity, the showerers (of desires), theadorable ( Maruts ), the possessors of wonderful strength.
The hills, oppressed and agitated by them, move (from their plural ces), the mountains are restraineḍ
(Their horses), quickly traversing (space), bear them travelling through the firmament, giving food to theworshipper.
Agni was born the first among the gods, like the brilliant sun in splendour; then they (the Maruts ) stoodround in their radiance.
8: Come to us, Aśvins , with all your protections; Dasras , riders in a golden chariot, drink the sweet Soma .
Aśvin , partakers of sacrificial food, decorated with golden ornaments, wise, and endowed with profoundintellects, come verily in your chariot, invested with solar radiance.
Come from (the world of) man, come from the firmament, (attracted) by our pious praises, drink, Aśvins ,the sweet Soma offered at the sacriice of the Kaṇvas .
Come to us from above the heaven, you who love the (world) below, (come) from the firmament; the sonof Kaṇva has been poured forth for you the sweet Soma libation.
Come, Aśvins , to drink the Soma at our sacrifice, you who are praised (by him) and honoured by hispious acts, benefactors of the worshipper, sages and leaders of rites.
Leaders of rites, when the Ṛṣis formerly invoked you for protection, you came; so now, Aśvins , comeat my devout praises.

Familiar with heaven, come to us from the sky, or from above the bright (firmament); favourably inclidedto the worshipper, (come), induced by his pious acts; hearers of invocations (come, induced) by our praiseṣ
What others than ourselves adore the Aśvins with praises? The Ṛṣi Vatsa , the son of Kaṇva , hasmagnified you with hymns.
The wise adorer invokes you hither with praise, Aśvins , for protection; sinless, utter destroyers ofenemies, be to us the sources of felicity.
Affluent in sacrifices, when the maiden ( sūrya ) mounted your chariot, then, Aśvins , you obtained allyour desires.
From wheresoever (you may be) come, Aśvins , with your thousandfold diversified chariot; the sageVatsa, the son of Kavi , has addressed you with sweet worlds.
Delighters of many, abonding in wealth, bestowers of riches, Aśvins , sustainers of all, approve of thismy adoration.
Grant us, Aśvins , all riches that may not bring us shame, make us the begetters of progeny in dueseason, subject us not to reproach.
Whether, Nāsatyās , you be far off, or whether you be near, come from there wiḥ your thousandolddiversified chariot.
Give, Nāsatyās , food of many kinds dripping with butter to him, the ṛṣi Vatsa , who has magnifiedyou both with hymns.
Give, Aśvins , invigorating food, dripping with butter, to him who praises you, the lords of liberality, toobtain happiness; who desires affluence.
Confounders of the malignant, partakers of many (oblations), come to this our adoration; render usprosperous leaders (of rites); give these (good things of earth) to our desires.
The Priyamedhas at the sacrifices to the gods invoke you, Aśvins , who rule over religious rites,together with your protections.
Come to us, Aśvins , sources of happiness, sources of health; (come), adorable (Aśvins), to that Vatsa ,who has magnified you with sacrifices and with praises.
Leaders (of rites), protect us with those protections with which you have protected Kaṇva andMedhātithi, Viśa and Daśavraja, with which you have protected Gośarya.
(And) with which, leaders (of rites), you protected Trasadasyu when wealth was to be acquired; do youwith the same graciously protec tus, Aśvins , for the acquisition of food.
May (perfect) hymns and holy praises magnify you, Aśvins ; protectors of many, exerminators of foes,greatly are you desired of us.
The three wheels (of the chariot) of he Aśvins , which were invisible, have become manifest; do youtwo, who are cognizant of the past, (come) by the paths of truth to the presence of living beings.
9: Come, Aśvins , without fail, for the protection of the worshipper; confer upon him a secure and spaciousdwelling; drive away those who make no offerings.
Whatever wealth may be in the firmament, in heaven, or among the five (classes) of men, bestow, Aśvins , (upon us).
Recognize, Aśvins , (the devotions0 of the son of Kaṇva , as (you have recognized) those former sageswho have repeatedly addresswed pious works to you.
This oblation is poured out, Aśvin , to you with praise; this sweet- savoured Soma is offered to you, whoare alluent with food, (animated) by which you meditate (the destruction) of the foe.
Doers of many deeds, Aśvins preserve me with that (healing virtue) deposited (by you) in the waters, inthe trees, in the herbs.
Although, Nāsatyās , you cherish (all beings), though, divinities, you heal (all disease),, yet this youradorer does not obtain you by praises (only), you go to him who offers you oblations.

When verily you arrive, Aśvins , the ṛṣi understands with excellent (comprehension) the praise (to beaddressed to you); he will sprinkle the sweet- flavoured Soma and the gharma (oblation) on Atharvan fire.
Abscond at once, Aśvins , your light-moving chariot; may these praises bring you down radiant as thesun.
Acknowledge Nāsatyās , that we may bring you down today by the prayers and he praises of the sonof Kaṇva .

Consider (my praises) in the same maner as (you have considered) when Kakṣīvat praied yo, whenthe ṛṣi Vyaśva , when Dīrghatamas , or Pṛthin, the son of Vena , glorified you in the chambers of sacrifice.
Come (to us as) guardians of our dwelling, become our defenders, be protectors of our dependants,cherishers of our person ns; come to the dwelling for (the good of) our sons and grandsons.

Although, Aśvins you should be riding in the same chariot with Indra , although you should be domiciledwith Vāyu , although you should be enjoying gratification along with the Ādityas and Ṛbhus , although you beproceeding on the tracks of Viṣṇu , (nevertheless come here).
Inasmuch as I invoke you, Aśvins , today for success in war (therefore grant it), for the triumphantprotection of the Aśvins is the most excellent for the destruction (of enemies) in battle.
Come, Aśvins , these libations are prepared for you; those libations which were presented you byTurvaśa and Yadu , they are now offered to you by Kaṇvas .
The healing drug, Nāsatyās , that is afar off or near, wherewith (you wen) to (his) dwelling for thesake of Vimada , do you who are of surpassing wisdom now grant to Vatsa .
I awake with the pious praise of the Aśvins ; scatter, goddess, (the darkness) at my eulogy; bestowwealth upon (us) mortals.
Uṣas, truht-speaking mighty goddess, awake the Aśvins ; invoker of the adorable (deities, arouse them)successively; the copious sacrificial food (is prepared) for their exhilaration.
When, Uṣas, you move with radiance, you shine equally with the sun; and this chariot of the Aśvinsproceeds to the hall of sacrifice frequented by the leaders (of the rite).
When the yellow Soma stalks milk forth as cows from their udders, when the devout (priests) repeat thewords of praise, then, O Aśvins , preserve us.
Endowed with great wisdom, preserve us for fame, for strength, for victory, for happiness, forprosperity.
Although, Aśvins , you be seated in the region of the paternal (heaven engaged in) holy rites, or,glorified by us, (abide there) with plural asures, (yet come here).
10: Whether, Aśvins , you are at present where the spacious halls of sacrifice (abound), whether you are inyonder bright sphere of heaven, or whether you are in a dwelling constructed above the firmament, come here.

In like manner, as you have prepared, Aśvins , the sacrifice for Manu , consent (to prepare it) for the sonof Kaṇva ; for I invoke Bṛhaspati , the universal gods, Indra and Viṣṇu , and the Aśvins, with rapid steeds.
I invoke those Aśvins , who are famed for great deeds, induced (to come here) for acceptance (of ouroblations), of whom among the gods the friendship is especially to be obtained.

Upon whom (all) sacrifices are dependent, of whom there are worshippers in a plural ce where is noworship, those two familiar with undecaying sacrifices (I invoke) with praises, that you may drink the sweet Soma .
Whether, Aśvins , you abide today in the west, whether opulent in food, you abide in the east, whetheryou sojourn with Druhyu , Anu, Turvaśu or Yadu , I invoke you, therefore, come to me.
Protectors of many, whether you traverse the firmament, or pass along earth and heaven, whether youascend your chariot with (all) your splendours, come from there, Aśvins , here.
11: Agni , who are a god among mortals, (and among gods), you are the guardian of religious obligations;you are to be hymned at sacrifices.
Victor (over enemies), you are to be hymned at solemn rites; you, Agni , are the charioteer of sacrifices.
Do you, Jātavedas , drive away from us those who hate us; (drive away), Agni , the impious hostilehosts.
You desire not, Jātavedas , the sacrifice of the man who is our adversary, although plural ced before you.
Prudent mortals, we offer abundant homage to you, who are immortal and all-knowing.
Prudent mortals, we invoke the sage deity Agni with hymns to propitiate him for our protection.
Vatsa , by the praise that seeks to propitiate you, Agni , would draw your thought from the supremeassembly (of the gods).
You look upon many plural ces, you are lord over all people; we call upon you in battles.
Desiring strength, we call upon Agni for protection in battles; upon him who is the granter of wonderfulriches (won) in conflicts.
You, the ancient, are to be hymned at sacrifices; from eternity the invoker of the gods, you sit (at thesolemnity) entitled to laudation; cherish, Agni , yor own person n, and grant us prosperity.
12: We solicit, most powerful Indra , who are the deep quaffer of the Soma , that exhilaration whichcontemplates (heroic deeds), whereby you slay the devourer (of men).
We solicit that (exhilaration) whereby you have defended Adhrigu , the accomplisher of the ten (monthśrite), and the trembling leader of heaven, (the sun), and the ocean.
We solicit that (exhilaration) whereby you urge on the mighty waters to the sea, in like manner as(charioteers drive) their cars (to the goal), and (whereby) to travel the paths of sacrifice.
Accepts, thunderer, their praise (offered) for the attainment of our desires, like consecrated butter;(induced) by which, you, promptly bear us by your might (to our objects).
Be plural ased, you who are gratified by praise, with this our eulogy swelling like the oceans, (induced bywhich), Indra , you ber us with all your proections (to our objects).
(I glorify Indra ) the deity, who, coming from afar, has given us, through friendship, (riches); heaping(them upon us) like rain from heaven, you have borne us (to our objects).
The banners of Indra , the thunderbolt (he bears) in his hands , have brought (us benefits), when, likethe sun, he has expanded heaven and earth.
Great Indra , protector of the good, when you have slain thousands of mighty (foes), then your vast andspecial energy has been augmented.
Indra , with the rays of the sun, utterly consumes his adversary; like fire (burning) the forests, hespreads victorious.
This new praise, suited to the season, approaches, ( Indra ), to you; offering adoration and greatlydelighting (you), it verily proclaims the measure (of your merits).

The devout praiser of the adorable ( Indra ) purifies in due succession the offering (of the Soma ); withsacred hymns he magnifies (the might) of Indra; he verily proclaims the measure (of hismerits).
Indra , the benefactor of his friend (the worshipper), has enlarged himself to drik the Soma , in likemanner as the pious praise dilates and proclaims the measure (of his merits).
I pour the oblation of the sacrifice, like clarified butter, into the mouth (of that Indra ), whom wise men,addressing with prayers, delight.
The excellent praise which Aditi brought forth for the imperial Indra , for our protection, is that which was(the product) of the sacrifice.
The bearers of the oblation glorify ( Indra ) for his excellent protection; now, divinity, let yourmany-actioned horses (bear you to the offering) of the sacrifice.
Inasmuch as you are exhilarated by the Soma shared with Viṣṇu , or when (offered) by Trita , the son ofthe waters, or along with the Maruts , so now (be gratified) by (our) libation.
Inasmuch, Śakra , as you are exhilarated (by the Soma ) on the far- distant ocean, so be you gratifiednow, when the Soma is effused by our libations.
Inasmuch, protector of the virtuous, as you are the benefactor of the worshipper offering you libations,or by whose prayers you are propitiated, so now (be gratified) by our libations.
I glorify the divine Indra wherever worshipped for your protection; (my praises) have reached him for theprompt (fulfilment) of the (objects of the) sacrifice.

(His worshippers) have magnified with many sacrifices him to whom the sacrifice is offered, and withmany libations the eager quaffer of the Soma ; (they have magnified) Indra with hymns, (their praises) haveattained him.
Infinite are his bounties, many are his glories; ample treasures have reached the donor (of oblations).
The gods have plural ced Indra (foremost) for the destruction of Vṛtra ; their praise has been addressed tohim to enhance his vigour.
We repeatedly glorify with praises and adorations him who is great with greatness, who hears ourinvocations, (to enhance) his vigour.
The thunderer, from whom neither the heaven and earth nor the firmament are separated; from thestrength of whom, the mighty one, (the world) derives lustre.
When, Indra , the gods plural ced you foremost in the battle, then your beloved horses bore you.
When, thunderer, by your strength you did slay Vṛtra , the obstructer of the waters, then your belovedhorses bore you.
When your (younger brother) Viṣṇu by (his) strength stepped his three paces, then verily your belovedhorses bore you.
When your beloved horses had augmented day by day, then all existent beings were subject unto you.
When, Indra , your people, the Maruts , were regulated by you, then all existent beings were subject untoyou.
Whenyou had plural ced yonder pure light, the sun, in the sky, then all existing beings were subject untoyou.
The wise (worshipper), Indra , offers you this gratifying sincere praise along with pious rites at thesacrifice, as (a man plural ces) a kinsman in (a prominent) position.
When the congregated (worshippers) praise him aloud in a plural ce that plural ases (him) on the navel (of theearth), in the spot where the libation is effused at the sacrifice, (then).
Bestow upon us, Indra , (wealth), comprising worthy male ofspring, excellent horses, and good cattle;like the ministrant priest (I worship you) at the sacrifice, (to secure) your prior consideration.
13: Indra , when the Soma juices are effused, sanctifies the offerer and the praiser for the attainment ofincrease giving strength, for he is mighty.
Abiding in the highest heaven, in the dwelling of the gods, he is the giver of increase, the accomplisher(of works), the possessor of great renown, the conqueror of (the obstructer of) the rains.
I invoke the powerful Indra for (aid in) the food-bestowing combat; be near unto us for our happiness;be a friend for our increase.
This gift of the offerer of the libation flows to you, Indra , who are gratified by praise, exhilarated bywhich you reign over the sacrifice.
Bestow upon us, Indra , that which, when pouring out the libation, we solicit of you; grant us thewondrous wealth that is the means of obtaining heaven.
When your discriminating eulogist has addressed to you overpowering praises, then, if they areacceptable to you, they expand like the branches (of a tree).
genitive rate your eulogies as of old; hear the invocation of the adorer; you bear in your reiteratedexultation (blessings) to the liberal donor (of the oblation).
The kind and true words of him who in this hymn is called the lord of heaven sport like waters flowingby a downward (channel).
Or he, who is called the one absolute lord of men-- praise him, when the libation is effused, withmagnifying songs, imploring his protection.
Praise the renowned, the sapient ( Indra ), whose victorious horses proceed to the dwelling of the devoutdonor (of the libation).
Munificently minded, do you, who are quick of movement, come with shining and swift steeds to thesacrifice, for verily there is gratification to you thereby.
Most powerful Indra , protector of the virtuous, secure us who praise you in the possession of riches,(grant) to the pious imperishable all-pervading sustenance.
I invoke you when the sun is risen; I invoke (you) at mid-day; being propitited, come to us, Indra , withyour gliding steeds.
Come quickly; hasten, be exhilarated by the libation mixed with milk; extend the ancient sacrifice, sothat I may obtain (its reward).
Whether, Śakra , you be far off, or, slayer of Vṛtra , near at hand , or whether you be in the firmament,you are the guardian of the (sacrificial) food.
May our praises magnify Indra ! May our effused libations gratify Indra! May the people bearingoblations excite plural asure in Indra!
The pious, desiring his protection, magnify him by ample and plural asure- yielding (libations); the earth,(and other worlds, spread out) like the branches of a tree, magnify Indra .
The gods propitiate the superintending adorable ( Indra ) at the Trikadruka rites. May our praisesmagnify him who is ever the magnifier (of his worshippers).
Your worshipper is observant of his duty, inasmuch as he offers prayers indue season; for you are hewho is called pure, purifying, wonderful.
The progeny of Rudra (the Maruts ) is known in ancient plural ces, and to them the intelligent worshippersoffer adoration.
If, ( Indra ), you choose my friendship, partake of this (sacrificial) food, by which we may pass beyond(the reach of) all adversaries.
When, Indra , who delight in praise, may your worshipper be entirely happy? When will you establish usin (the affluence of) cattle, of horses, of dwellings?
Or, when will your renowned and vigorous horses bring the chariot of you, who are exempt from decay,that exhilarating (wealth) which we solicit?
We solicit with ancient and gratifying (offerings) him who is mighty and the invoked of many; may he sitdown on the plural asant sacred grass, and accept the two-fold (offering of cakes and Soma ).
Praised of many, prosper (us) with the protections hymned by the ṛṣis, send down upon us nutritiousfood.
Thunderbolt-bearing Indra , you are the protector of him who thus eulogises you; I seek through sacrificefor your favour, which is to be gained by praise.
Harnessing your horses, Indra , laden with treasure and sharing your exhilaratio, come here to drink ofthe Soma .
May the sons of Rudra , who are your followers, approach and partake of the glory (of the sacrifice); andmay (other celestial) people associated with the Maruts (partake of the sacrificial) food.

May those who (are his attndants), victorious (over enemies), be satisfied with the station (which theyoccupy) in heaven, and may they be assembled at the navel of the sacrifice, that I may therefrom acquire(wealth).
When the ceremony is being prepared in the hall of sacrifice, this ( Indra ), having inspected the rite,regulates (the performance) in due succession for a distant object.

Your chariot, Indra , is a showerer (of benefits), showerers (of benefits) are your horses; you alsoŚatakratu, are the showerer (of benefits) the invocation (addressed to you) is the showerer (of benefits).

The stone (that bruises the Soma ) is the showerer (of benefits), so is your exhilaration and this Somathat is effused; the sacrifice that you accept is the showerer (of benefits),such also is your invocation.

The showerer (of the oblation) I invoke with manifold and gratifying (praises) you, O thunderer, theshowerer (of benefits); inasmuch as you acknowledge the eulogy addressed to you, your invocation is theshowerer (of benefits).
14: If, Indra , I were, as you are, sole, lord over wealth, then should my eulogist be possessed of cattle.
Lord of might, I would give to that intelligent worshipper that which I should wish to give, if I were thepossessor of cattle.
Your praise, Indra , is a cow to the worshipper offering the libations, it milks him in abundance cattle andhorses.
Neither god nor man, Indra , is the obstructor of your affluence, (of) the wealth which you, when praised,design to bestow.
Sacrifice has magnified Indra , so that he has supported the earth (with rain), making (the cloud)quiescent in the firmament.
We solicit, Indra , the protection of you, who are ever being magnified, the conqueror of all the riches (ofthe enemy).
In the exhilaration of the Soma , Indra has traversed the radiant firmament that he might pierce (theasura) Vala .
He liberated the cows for the aṅgirasas , making manifest those that have been hidden in the cave,hurling Vala headlong down.
By Indra the constellations were made stable and firm and stationary, so that they could not be movedby any.
Your praise, Indra , mounts aloft like the exulting wave of the waters, your exhilarations have beenmanifested.
You, Indra , are to be magnified by praise, you are to be magnified by prayer; you are the benefactor ofthose who praise you.
Let the long-maned horses bring the wealth-bestowing Indra to the sacrifice to drink the Soma .
You have struck off, Indra , the head of Namuci with the foam of the waters, when you had subdued allyour enemies.
You have hurled down, Indra , the Dasyus , gliding upwards by their devices and ascending to heaven.
You, Indra , the most excellent drinker of the Soma , destroy the adverse assembly that offers nolibations.
15: Glorify him the invoked of many, the praised of many; adore the powerful Indra with hymns.
The vast strength of whom, powerful in both (regions), has sustained the heaven and earth, and by itsvigour (upheld) the swift clouds and flowing waters.
You, the praised of many, reign; you, single, have slain many enemies, in order to acquire the spoils ofvictory and abundant food.
We celebrate, thunderer, your exhilaration, the showerer (of benefits), the overcomer (of foes) in battle,the maker of the world, the glorious with your steeds.
Whereby you have made the plural nets manifest to Ayu and to Manu , and rule rejoicing over this sacredrite.
The reciters of prayer celebrate that your (exhilaration) now as of old; do you daily hold in subjectionthe waters, the wives of the showerer.
Praise sharpens your great energy, your strength, your acts, and your majestic thunderbolt.
The heaven invigorates your manhood, Indra , the earth (spreads) your renown; the waters, themountains propitiate you.
Viṣṇu , the mighty giver of dwellings, praises you, and Mitra and Varuṇa ; the company of the Marutsimitates you in exhilaration.
You, Indra , who are the showerer, have been born the most bountiful of beings; you associate with youall good offspring.
( Indra ), the praised of many, you alone destroy many mighty foes; no other Indra achieves such greatexploits.
When (in the combat), Indra , they invoke you in many ways with praise for protection, then do you (soinvoked) by our leaders overcome all (our enemies).
All the forms (of Indra ) have sufficiently entered into our own spacious abode; gratify Indra the lord ofŚacī, (that he may give us) the spoil of victory.
16: Glorify with hymns the adorable Indra , the supreme king of men, the leader (of rites), the overcomer ofenemies, the most munificent.
In whom all praises, all kinds of sustenance concentrate, like the aggregation of the waters in theocean.
I worship Indra with pious praises, glorious among the best (of beings), the achiever of great deeds inwar mighty for the acquisition (of wealth).
Whose unbounded and profound exhilarations are many, protective, and animating in waṛ
(His worshippers) invoke him to take part (in spoiling) the trasures deposited (with the foe); theyconquer, of whom Indra is (the partisan).
They honour him with animating (hymns), men (honour) him with sacred rites, for Indra is the giver ofwealth.
Indra is Brahmā , Indra is the ṛṣi; Indra is the much-invoked of many, mighty with mighty deeds.
He is to be praised, he is to be invoked, he is true, powerful the doer of many deeds; he, being single,is the overcomer (of his foes).
Men who are cognizant (of sacred texts) magnify Indra with pious precepts, with sacred songs, and withprayers.
Him (they magnify) who brings before them the spoil, who gives lustre in combats, who overcomesenemies in battle.
May Indra , the fulfiller (of desires), the invoked of many, bear us beyond (the reach of) all our enemies,to welfare, as if by a ship (across the sea).
Do you, Indra , (endow) us with vigour, bestow upon us (wealth, enable us) to go (by the right way), leadus to felicity.
17: Come, we express, Indra , for you, the Soma ; drink it; sit down upon this my sacred grass.
Let your long-maned horses, Indra , that are yoked by prayers, bring you here, anddo you hear ourprayers.
We brāhmaṇas , offerers of Soma , bearing the effused Soma, invoke with suitable (prayers), you thedrinker of the Soma.
Come to us offering the libation, accept our earnest praises; drink, handsome-jawed, of the (sacrificial)beverage.
I fill your belly (with the libation); let is spread throughout the limbs; take the honied Soma with yourtongue.
May the sweet-flavoured Soma be grateful to you, who are munificent; (may it be grateful) to your bodymay it be exhilarating to your heart.
May this Soma , invested (with milk), approach you, observant Indra , like a bride (clad in white apparel).
Long-necked, large-bellied, strong-armed Indra , in the exhilaration of the (sacrificial) food, destroys hisenemies.
Indra , who by your strength are the lord over all, come to us, slayer of Vṛtra , subdue our foes.
Long be your goad, wherewith you bestow wealth upon the sacrificer offering libations.
This Soma , purified (by filtering) through the sacred grass is for you, Indra , come to it, hasten, drink.
Renowned for radiance, renowned for adoration, this libation is for your gratification; destroyer of foes,you are earnestly invoked.
( Indra ), who was the offspring of Śṛṅgavṛṣa, of whom the kuṇḍapāyya rite was the protector, (thesages) have fixed (of old) their minds upon this ceremony.

Lord of dwellings, may the (roof) pillar be strong; may there be vigour of body for the offerers of libation;may Indra , the drinker (of the Soma ), the destroyer of the numerous cities (of the asuras ), ever be the friend ofthe Munis .

With head uplifted like a serpent, adorable, the recoverer of the cattle, Indra single, is superior tomultitudes; (the worshipper) brings Indra to drink the Soma by a rapid seizure, like a loaded horse (by a halter).
18: Let a mortal now earnestly solicit at the worship of these Ādityas unprecedented riches.
The paths of these Ādityas are unobstructed and unopposed; may they yield us security and augmentour happiness.
May Savitā , Bhaga , Varuṇa , Mitra , and Aryaman bestow upon us that ample felicity which we solicit.
Divine Aditi , bringer of safety, beloved of many, com propitiously with the wise and happy divinitieṣ
These sons of Aditi know how to drive away (our) enmies; and, doers of great deeds and donors ofsecurity, (they know how to extricate us) from sin.
May Aditi protect our cattle by day, ad, free from duplicity (guard them) by night; may Aditi, by herconstant favour, preserve us from sin.
May the monitress Aditi come to us, for our prosecution by day; may she grant us tranquil felicity, andlive away, (our) enemies.
May the two divine physicians, the Aśvins , grant us health; may they drive away from hence iniquity;(may they drive) away our foes.
May the two divine physicians, the Aśvins , grant us health; may they drive away from hence iniquity;(may they drive) away our foes.
Ādityas , remove (from us) disease, enemies, malignity; keep us afar from sin.
Keep afar from us, Ādityas , malignity, ill-will; do you who are all- wise keep afar those who hate us.
Grant freely to us, genitive rous Ādityas , that happiness which liberates even the offending (worshipper)from sin.
May that man who, from his diabolical nature seeks to do us evil-- may he, injuring himself by his owndevices, incu that evil.
May iniquity pervade hat calumniating and hostile mortal who wishes to do us harm, and is treacheroustowards us.
Deities, you are (propitious) to sincere (worshippers), you know, Vasus , the hearts of men, anddistinguish between the single and double-minded.
We solicit the happiness of the mountains and of the waters; heaven and earth, remove sin far from us.
Convey us, Vasus , in your vessel, with auspicious felicity, beyond all calamities.
Radiant Ādityas grant to our sons and grandsons to enjoy long life.
The duly-presented sacrifice is ready for you, Ādityas ; grant us, therefore, happiness; may we everabide in near relationship with you.
We solicit of the divine protector of he Maruts , of the Aśvisn, of Mitra and of Varuṇa , a spaciousdwelling for our welfare.
Mitra , Aryaman , Varuṇa and Maruts , grant us a secure, excellent and well-peopled dwelling, athree-fold shelter.
Since, Ādityas , we mortals are of kin to death, do you benevolently (exert yourselves to) prolong ourlives.
19: Glorify ( Agni ), the leader of all (sacred rites); the priests approach the divine lord, (and through him)convey the oblation to the gods.
Praise, pious Sobhari, at the sacrifice this ancient Agni , who is the giver of opulence, the wonderfullyluminous, the regulator of this rite, at which the Soma is presented.
We adore you, the most adorable deity, the invoker of the gods, the immortal, the perfecter of thissacrifice.

Agni , the great grandson of (sacrificial) food, the possessor of opulence, the illuminator, the shedder ofexcellent light; may he obtain for us by sacrifice the happiness in heaven (that is the gift) of Mitra , of Varuṇa , ofthe waters.
The man who has presented (worship) to Agni with fuel, with burnt offerings, with the Veda , with(sacrificial) food, and is diligent in pious rites.
Of him assuredly the rapid horses rush (on the foe); his is most brilliant glory; him no evil, whether thework of gods or of men, ever assails.
Son of strength, lord of (sacrificial) food, may we be favoured with your various fires; do you, ( Agni ),endowed with energy, be well-disposed towards us!

Agni , when honoured like a guest, is gracious to his praisers; he is to be recognized as a chariot(bringing the fruit of the worship); in you verily the virtuous are confiding; you are the rājā of riches.
Agni , may he who is the offerer of sacrifice obtain his reward; he, auspicious Agni, is worthy ofcommendation; may he by his pious rites become the giver of wealth.
He whose sacrifice you preside, prospers, having his dwelling filled with male offspring; he is theeffecter of his purposes through his horses, through his wise (counsellors), his valiant adherents.
(So is he) in whose dwelling the all-desired and embodied Agni receives praise and food, and conveysoblations to the all-pervading deities.
Son of strength, giver of dwellings, plural ce the prayer of he devout intelligent worshipper, who is mostprompt in offerings, below the gods and above mortals.
He who propitiated the powerful and quick radiating Agni with offerings of oblations, with reverentialadorations and with praise, (is prosperous).
The mortal who propitiates Aditi with his ( Agni 's) many forms by blazing fuel, prospering through hispious rites, shall surpass all men in renown as (if he had crossed over) the waters.
Bestow upon us, Agni , that power which may overcome any cannibal (entering) into our abode, thewrath of any malignant (being).
Protected by Indra , well-knowing the path that through your power, ( Agni ), we should follow, we adorethat (radiance) of you, by which Varuṇa , Mitra , Aryaman , the Nāsatyās , and Bhaga shine.
Those verily, Agni , are of approved piety who as your worshippers, sagacious deity, have establishedyou as the contemplator of men, the perfomer of good works.

Auspicious ( Agni ), they have set up the altar, have presented oblations, have expressed the libation ona (fortunate) day; they have won by their efforts infinite wealth who have plural ced their affection upon you.
May Agni , to whom burnt-offerings have been made, be propitious to us; auspicious (Agni), may yourgifts be blessings, may the sacrifice (we offer) be beneficial, may our praises yield us happiness.
Give us that resolute mind in conflict by which you conquer in combats; humble the many firm (resolves)of our foes; may we propitiate you by our sacrifices.
I worship Agni , who has been established by Manu with praise, whom the gods have appointed theirroyal messenger, who is the most adorable, the bearer of oblations.
Offer (sacriicial) food to that bright-shining, every-youthful, royal Agni , who, (when gratified) by sincerepraises, and worshipped with oblations, bestows excellent male offspring.
When Agni , worshipped with oblations, sends his voice upwards and downwards, as the sun disperseshis rays, (we praise him).

The divine ( Agni ), established by Manu , the offerer of the sacrifice, the invoker (of the gods), the divine,the immortal, who conveys the oblations in his fragrant mouth, bestows (upon his adorers) desirable (riches).
Agni , son of strength, shining with friendly radiance, and worshipped with oblations, may I, who,although mortal, am as you are, become immortal.

May I not be accusative ed, Vasu , of calumniating you, nor, gracious ( Agni ), of sinfulness (against you); letnot (the priest) the reciter of my praises be dull of intellect or ill-disposed; (may he not err), Agni, throughwickedness.
Cherished by us as a son by a father, let him ( Agni ) in our dwelling convey promptly our oblation to thegods.
Agni , granter of dwellings, may I, who am mortal, ever enjoy plural asure through your proximateprotections.
May I propitiate you, Agni , by worshipping you, by the gifts presented to you, by your praises; verily, Vasu , they have called you the benevolent- minded; delight, Agni, to give me wealth.
He, Agni , whose friendship you accept, prospers through your favours, granting male progeny andample food.

Sprinkled, ( Agni , with the libation), the dripping ( Soma ), car-borne, agreeable, offered in due season,resplendent, have been presented to you; you are the beloved of the mighty dawns; you reign over the things ofnight.
We, the Sobharis, have come to the thousand-rayed, the sincerely- worshipped, the universalsovereign, the ally of Trasadasyu , for his protection.
Agni , on whom your other fires are dependent, like branches (on the stem of the tree), may I amongmen, magnifying your powers, become possessed, like (other) votaries, of (abundant) food.
Benevolent and genitive rous Ādityas , amid all the offerers of oblations, the man whom you conduct to thelimit (of his undertakings obtains his reward).

Royal ( Ādityas ), overcomers of (hostile) men, (you subdue) any one harassing those (who areengaged in sacred rites) and may we, Varuṇa , Mitra , and Aryaman , be the conveyers of the sacrifice(addressed) to you.
The magnificent lord, the protector of the virtuous, Trasadasyu , the son of Purukutsa , has given me fivehundred brides.
The affluent Śyāva , the lord of kine, has given to me upon the banks of Suvastu a present of seventythree (cows).
20: Far-travellig (winds), alike wrathful, come here, harm us not; benders of the solid (mountains), withdrawnot from us.
Mighty sons of Rudra , Maruts , come with brilliant, strong-wheeled (chariots); desired of many,well-disposed to Sobhari, come today to our sacrifice with (abundant) food.
We know the great strength of the active sons of Rudra , the Maruts , the shedders of the diffusive raiṇ

They fall upon the island; the firm-set (trees) are with difficulty sustained; they agitate both heaven andearth; they urge on the waters; bright- weaponed, far-shining, whatever (you approach) you cause to tremble.
At your coming the unprecipitated mountains and trees resound; the earth shakes at your passage.
(Alarmed) at your violence, Maruts , the heaven seeks to rise higher, abandoning the firmament, where(you) the strong-armed leaders (of rites) display the ornaments of (your) person ns.
The radiant, strong, rain-shedding, undisguised leaders of rites display their great glory when acceptingthe (sacrificial) food.

The voice (of the Maruts ) blends with the songs of the Sobharis in the receptacle of their goldenchariot; may the mighty well-born Maruts, the offspring of the (bridled) cow, (be gracious) to us regard of food,enjoyment, and kindness.
Sprinklers of the libation, present the offerings to the rain-bestowing swift-passing company of theMaruts.
Maruts , leaders (of rites), come like swift-flying birds in your rain- shedding, strong-horsed chariot,whose wheels bestow showers, to partake of our oblations.
Their decoration is the same; gold (necklaces) shine (on their breasts), lances gleam upon theirshoulders.
Fierce, vigorous, strong-armed, they need not exert (the energy of their) person ns; bows and arrows areready in your chariots; the glory (of conquest) over (hostile) armies is yours.
One illustrious name is given to them all, as widely diffused as water for the gratification (of theirworshippers), like invigoraing paternal food.

Praise them, praise the Maruts , for we are (dependen) upon those agitators (of all things) as a menial isupon his lords; therefore are their donations (characterized) by munificence; such are their (gifts).
Fortunate was he, Maruts , who, in former days, was secure in your protections, as is he who nowenjoys them.
The sacrificer, to partake of whose oblations you approach, leaders of rites, enjoys, agitators of allthings, the felicity you bestow, together with abundant viands, and the gift of strength.
May this (our praise) take effect, so that the ever-youthful sons of Rudra , creators of the cloud,(coming) from heaven, may be plural ased with us.
Youthful ( Maruts ), approaching us with benevolent hearts, grant prosperity to those liberal men whoworship you, who zealously propitiate you, the showerers of rain, with oblations.
Praise, Sobhari, (and attract here) by a new song the youthful purifying showerers, as (a plural ughman)repeatedly drags his oxen.

Propitiate wiḥ praise he Maruts , the senders of rain, the givers of plural asure, the liberal bestowers offood; who are ever victorious in combats, and like a boxer who has been challenged over his challengerṣ
Maruts , who are of like wrath, offspring of the maternal cow ( Pṛśni ), related by a common origin, theyseverally spread through the quarters of the horizon.

Maruts , dancing (through the air), decorated with golden breast-plural tes, the mortal (who worships you)attains your brotherhood; speak favourably to us, for your affinity is ever (made known) at the regulated(sacrifice).
genitive rous fiends, Maruts , swift gliding (through the air), bring to us (the boon) of the medicaments thatbelong to your company.

With those auspicious protectionw with which you have guarded the ocean, with which you havedesroyed (your enemies), with which you provided the well (for Gotama ), do you who are he sources ofhappiness, the unconquerable by your adversaries, bestow happiness upon uṣ]The unconquerable:asasacadviṣa = śatrurahitaḥ, destitute of enemies].
Whatever medicament there may be in the Sindhu , the Asikni , in the oceans, in the mountains, Maruts ,who are gratified by sacrifice.

Do you, beholding every sort, collect them for (the good of) our bodies, ad instrumental uct us in their (uses); letthe cure of sickness (be the portion), Maruts , of him among us who for his wickedness is sick; re-establish hisenfeebled (frame).
21: Unpreceded Indra , cherishing you (with sacrificial food), desirous of your protection, we invoke you whoare manifold in battle, as (men call upon) some stout (person n for help).
We have recourse, Indra , to you for protection at sacred rites; may he who is ever young, fierce,resolute, come to us! We, your friends, Indra, rely upon you as our protector and benefactor.
Lord of horses, of cattle, of corn-land, these libations (are for you); come, lord of the Soma , drink theeffused Soma.
Intelligent, but destitute of kin, let us connect ourselves, Indra , with you, who abound with kinsmen;come, showerer (of benefits), with all your glories, to drink the Soma .
Gathering like (a flock of) birds round your exhilarating heaven- bestowing Soma mixed with curds, werepeatedly glorify you, Indra .

We salute you with this adoration; why do you so often mediate (upon our requests)? Master of baysteeds, let our desires be granted. You are their bestower, we are your (suppliants) and our sacred rites are(addressed to you).
We verily are the most recent (objects) of your protection, Indra , wielder of the thunderbolt, we have notknown of old one greater than you.

We acknowledge, hero, your friendship, (the wealth) to be enjoyed through you, and solicit both,thunderer, of you; giver of dwellings, Indra of the handsome jaws, sustain us in all abundance and in (store of)cattle.
I glorify friends, for your protection, that Indra who has brought to us of old this or that excellent(wealth).

That man glorifies Indra , the lord of bay steeds, the protector of the good, the overcomer of enemies,who rejoices (in the fulfilment of his wishes); may Maghavan bestow upon us, his worshippers, hundreds of cattleand horses.
With you, showerer (of benefits), for our ally, we bid defiance to one assailing us in a contest (onbehalf) of a man possessing herds of cattle.

Indra , invoked of many, may we conquer in battle those contending against us; may we resist themalignant; may we, aided by the leaders (of rites, the Maruts ), slay Vṛtra ; may we be prosperous, and do youprotect our pious works.
You, Indra , are by your birth brotherless; from ever are you without a kinsman; the kindred you desire is(that of him) who engages in war.

You acknowledge no friendship for the wealthy man (who makes no offerings); those who are puffed upwith wine offered you; when you instrumental tute (the sacrifice), you expelled niggardliness, and you are invoked as aprotector.
Let us not, like fools, Indra , be regardless of the friendship of such as you are; let us assemble togetherwhen the libation is effused.

Let us never, Indra , giver of cattle, cease (to benefit) from your wealth; let us not accept it (from anotherthan) you; do you, who are the lord, connfirm to us permanent (riches), bestow them upon us; your benefactionscannoe be arrested.
Is it Indra who has given to the donor (of the oblation) so much affluence? Is it the auspiciousSarasvatī (who has given) the treasure? Or, Citra , is it you?

Verily the Rājā Citra , giving his thousands and tens of thousands, has overspread (with his bounty)those other petty princes, who rules along the Sarasvatī , as Parjanya (overspeads the earth) with rain.
22: I invoke to-day for our protection that splendid chariot, which, adorable Aśvins , advancing on the pathto battle, you ascended (to go to the wwedding) of Sūrya .

Celebrate, Sobhari, with praises (that chariot), the benefactor of former (encomiasts), the worthilyinvoked, the desired of many, the preserver, the foremost in battles, the relied upon by all, the scatterer ofenemies, the exempt from ill.
We incite by our adorations on this occasion the two divine Aśvins , the overcomers of foes, that theymay come down for our protection and proceed to the dwelling of the donor (of the offering).
One of the wheels of your car moves in every direction; the other, impellers of actions, remains withyou; may your favour, lords of rain, hasten towards us as a cow (to her calf)!
Your celebrated chariot, Aśvins , that is three-banked, and caparisoned with gold, graces heaven andearth; come with it, Nāsatyās .

Bestowing upon Manu the ancient (rain) from the firmament, you enabled him to cultivate (the soil) withthe plural ugh (and reap) the barley; now therefore, Aśvins , lords of rain, we glorify you both with praises.
Rich in food, Aśvins , come to us by the paths of sacrifice, those by which showerers (of benefits), youwent to gratify Tṛkṣi, the son of Trasadasyu , with vast wealth.
Leaders (of rites), affluent in rain, this Soma has been expressed by the (grinding) stones for you; cometo drink the Soma, drink it in the dwelling of the donor.
Aśvins , who are rich in rain, ascend your golden chariot, a storehouse (of weapons); bring to usfattening food.
With those protections with which you have defended Paktha , Adhrigu , and Babhru , when propitiatingyou, come to us, Aśvins , quickly; administer medicine to the sick.
At the tiem when hurrying, devout, we invoke you both speedily going to battle, at the dawn of day, withour hymns.

Then, showerers, come to my manifold all-propitiating invocation with those (protections), with which,leaders (of rites), you, who are gratified (by oblations), munificent (in gifts), and the overcomers of numerous(foes), gave augmentation to the well; with such (protections) come here.
I address the Aśvins , glorifying them at break of day; we solicit them with oblations.

We adore those lords of water, leaders on the road of battle, in the evening, at dawn, and at mid-day;therefore, Rudras who are rich in food, give us not up hereafter to a mortal adversary; rudravartanī : yuddherodanaśilamārgau stūyamānamārgau vā].
Adorable Aśvins , bring in your chariot at early dawn happiness to me, soliciting happiness; I, Sobhari,invoke you as (did my) father.
